operational_criterion_R1: A connection end is defective iff, after resolving its feature chain, it denotes more than one feature (the chain traverses a usage whose multiplicity admits more than one instance), so the connector as written does not relate individual features.

items.spec_basis: SatisfyRequirementUsage textual production (SysML 2.0 §8.2.2.21.2): the notation is 'satisfy <requirement> by <feature>' — neither 'to' nor the reversed operand order is admitted, so the text is not in the language.
items.independent_corroboration: second coder assigned the same class to this text; corroboration is WEAK because the coder-facing codebook contained this excerpt verbatim or its exemplar (see coding/agreement-addendum.md)
items.notes: Operand order reversed and 'to' used instead of 'by'; the notation is 'satisfy <req> by <feature>'. confidence=high

items.spec_basis: No constraint relates documentation to declared values (deriveElementDocumentation, §8.3.2.1.2, relates documentation to content only). Basis is an authored reading, and it is contested.
items.evidence_excerpt: doc /* Soil moisture shall be kept between 35% and 75% ... */ / attribute upperBound : Real = 55.0;
items.contested_note: Rival reading accepted as live: a documentation band of 35-75 % contains the declared 35-55 % bound, so a tightened engineering limit is not a contradiction on its face. The record is kept (fixed before detection) and marked contested; report with and without it.
items.independent_corroboration: no independent corroboration (this model was not double-coded)
items.notes: The requirement's own documentation and its own attribute declare different upper bounds. The prompt-fidelity deviation is NOT counted (exclusion 1). confidence=high

items.spec_basis: States textual notation, transition productions (SysML 2.0 §8.2.2.18): a transition states its ends as 'transition first <source> … then <target>'. 'from … to … on …' is SysML v1/UML notation and is not admitted.
items.evidence_excerpt: transition from idle to lowering on detection.approaching;
items.independent_corroboration: second coder assigned the same class to this text; corroboration is WEAK because the coder-facing codebook contained this excerpt verbatim or its exemplar (see coding/agreement-addendum.md)
items.notes: 4 occurrences (lines 48-51) of SysML v1/UML 'from ... to ... on/when' transition notation. Names inside the unparsed spans (detection, leftArm) are not double-coded (precedence 2). confidence=high

items.spec_basis: checkSatisfyRequirementUsageBindingConnector (§8.3.21.10), a discretionary MAY constraint: a SatisfyRequirementUsage must have exactly one BindingConnector between its subject and a satisfying feature. The textual production (§8.2.2.21.2) makes the 'by' clause optional, so this is a constraint-layer, not a notation, defect.
items.independent_corroboration: second coder assigned the same class to this text; corroboration is WEAK because the coder-facing codebook contained this excerpt verbatim or its exemplar (see coding/agreement-addendum.md)
items.notes: The 'by' clause is OPTIONAL in the BNF (SysML 2.0 formal/2026-03-02, 8.2.2.21.2), so this is not a parse defect: it is a satisfy usage with no satisfying feature, violating the discretionary check constraint that requires a binding from the subject parameter. Relabelled from syntax/blocking to constraint/minor in codebook v1.1 after the BNF was retrieved. confidence=high (grammar read directly)

items.spec_basis: Basis: the model uses SysML/KerML standard-library scalar types with no library import. The normative model libraries declare Real/Boolean; no named constraint requires the import.
items.independent_corroboration: no independent corroboration (this model was not double-coded)
items.notes: No library import at all; 10 occurrences (6x Real, 4x Boolean) are unresolved standard-library scalar types. Counted once per model (coding unit). confidence=high

items.spec_basis: Reserved-keyword list (SysML 2.0 §8.2.2.1.2) applied to the ID terminal: 'in' and 'out' are reserved keywords and cannot be written as unquoted feature names in a port declaration; line 33 references the illegal name.
items.independent_corroboration: second coder assigned the same class to this text; corroboration is WEAK because the coder-facing codebook contained this excerpt verbatim or its exemplar (see coding/agreement-addendum.md)
items.notes: 'in' is a reserved feature-direction keyword used as a declared port name (line 23) and then referenced as a chain (line 33, line.in). 2 occurrences, one mechanism. confidence=medium

items.spec_basis: No named OCL constraint covers name resolution. Basis: the identifier used in this construct is declared nowhere in scope (name resolution, SysML 2.0 §7.5 / KerML §8.3.2.4). For the satisfy-target records the name is the requirement definition's subject parameter, which is a feature of the definition and not of the package.
items.independent_corroboration: second coder assigned the same class to this text; corroboration is WEAK because the coder-facing codebook contained this excerpt verbatim or its exemplar (see coding/agreement-addendum.md)
items.notes: 'pump' exists only as the subject parameter of requirement def AlarmTiming (line 37); there is no part usage pump in the package, so the satisfy's satisfying feature does not resolve. confidence=high

items.spec_basis: InitialNodeMember: 'first' takes memberFeature = [QualifiedName], a cross-reference to a feature (SysML 2.0 §8.2.2.17.2). The referenced name resolves to an action DEFINITION (a type), not a feature/usage, so the succession cannot be formed.
items.evidence_excerpt: first checkCharge; / then checkAvailability; / then assign;
items.independent_corroboration: second coder assigned the same class to this text; corroboration is WEAK because the coder-facing codebook contained this excerpt verbatim or its exemplar (see coding/agreement-addendum.md)
items.notes: checkCharge, checkAvailability and assign are declared as action DEFINITIONS at lines 47-49; a succession requires action USAGES. 3 occurrences, one mechanism. confidence=medium

items.spec_basis: End-feature multiplicity conformance: after resolving the feature chain the end denotes more than one feature, so it is not 1..1. Nearest named rule validateFeatureEndMultiplicity (KerML §8.3.3.3.4, SHOULD); §7.13.2 states the same for connection ends. No named constraint decides chains over multi-valued usages: this is an authored criterion, stated below. Criterion: a connection end is defective iff, after resolving its feature chain, it denotes more than one feature.
items.evidence_excerpt: connection powerLink connect controller.fleet.battery.power to controller.fleet.dock.power;
items.contested_note: Defect status not disputed; layer contested between type/typing (end-feature multiplicity conformance, the recorded reading) and structural/architectural (the rival reading).
items.independent_corroboration: second coder assigned the same class to this text; corroboration is WEAK because the coder-facing codebook contained this excerpt verbatim or its exemplar (see coding/agreement-addendum.md)
items.notes: fleet is Agv[10]; the connector end traverses a multi-valued usage, so the connector does not relate individual features. No named constraint decides chains over multi-valued usages, so this is coded as a structural defect from the model text. confidence=medium
